html:
In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • Run mode, Start: the level completes (hopper empty, belt clear)
  • Every bottle in the right bin, none lost
  • Under par (145 s)

Hard · par 145 s

The job

Three machines on one line: the unscrambler, the filler and the capper, with an accumulation table between each pair. The filler is the key machine: fixed at 60 bottles a minute, and the line is judged by it; it fills each bottle from Product_Tank and the capper caps it; Good_Bin takes filled and capped bottles. Every second it stands starved (nothing at its infeed) or blocked (its discharge backed up) is output the line never gets back; each time it stops costs 20 points. The unscrambler's supply runs thin now and then, and the capper's cap chute jams now and then. Each table has three eyes, Full, High and Low: a bottle standing in front of one for half a second says the table has backed up to it (a bottle flowing past only covers it for a moment). At Start the tables are empty: let the filler's table fill before the filler starts. Step the unscrambler's and the capper's speeds (Speed_Ref, bottles a minute, up to 90) so the filler stays fed and clear: faster either side of it, the V-curve. Hold a machine before it runs blocked: three seconds blocked and line pressure tips bottles over (a fault, −50, Reset to clear). The HMI shows the line: each machine's speed as a share of the filler's, its state, the tables, and the filler's efficiency. +100 a bottle into Good_Bin.

The program

Each table eye is debounced with a half-second timer, so it reads a table backed up to it and not a bottle flowing past. The unscrambler runs fast short of the low eye, at the V-curve speed between the eyes and at the filler’s speed past the high eye, and is held when its table is full until it drains below the high eye. The filler is held when the capper’s table backs up to it. The capper runs fast past its high eye, at the V-curve speed between the eyes and at the filler’s speed short of the low eye. Start resets the machines’ faults.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

The rungs

Watch for

A machine that runs blocked for three seconds tips bottles over. Hold a machine on the eye in front of the full table, not on the jam it causes.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens. A run of this program on v2.02 completed in about 136 s against a par of 145 s, with 12160 points and nothing wrong.

rungs.head: Rung 0

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The conveyor runs under the tables the whole time: the machines meter the bottles, the tables let them stand nose to tail
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Conv_Run (The line conveyor under all three machines and the tables: it runs with the line) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Conv_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conv_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: THE ACCUMULATION EYES, DEBOUNCED. A bottle flowing past covers an eye for a fifth of a second; bottles standing nose to tail cover it for good. Half a second covered means the line has backed up to the eye

pred.q: PE_A_Full is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: T_A_Full is reset to 0. It stops at XIC(PE_A_Full).

rungs.words: When PE_A_Full (Accumulation eye A Full: a bottle in front of it) is on, the rung runs the timer T_A_Full (Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) toward 500 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_A_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_A_Full is on.
  2. TON(T_A_Full,500,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_A_Full toward 500 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_A_Full counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: THE UNSCRAMBLER'S SPEED, from how far its accumulation has backed up. Short of the low eye the filler is close to starving: fast, 90 bpm (150 % of the filler)

pred.q: T_A_Low.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: U_Speed is written.

rungs.words: When T_A_Low.DN (the done bit of T_A_Low: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung puts 90 into U_Speed (Unscrambler: speed reference, bottles a minute).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(T_A_Low.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_A_Low.DN is off.
  2. MOV(90,U_Speed) Move does: puts 90 into U_Speed. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: between the low and high eyes: the normal V-curve speed, 69 bpm (115 %), a little faster than the filler so the table refills after a hiccup
rungs.words: When T_A_Low.DN (the done bit of T_A_Low: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on and T_A_High.DN (the done bit of T_A_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung puts 69 into U_Speed (Unscrambler: speed reference, bottles a minute).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_A_Low.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_A_Low.DN is on.
  2. XIO(T_A_High.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_A_High.DN is off.
  3. MOV(69,U_Speed) Move does: puts 69 into U_Speed. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: past the high eye: down to the filler's own speed, 60 bpm, so the table holds where it is

pred.q: T_A_High.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: U_Speed is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(T_A_High.DN).

rungs.words: When T_A_High.DN (the done bit of T_A_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on, the rung puts 60 into U_Speed (Unscrambler: speed reference, bottles a minute).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_A_High.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_A_High.DN is on.
  2. MOV(60,U_Speed) Move does: puts 60 into U_Speed. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: FULL: hold the unscrambler. Running blocked would push the table until bottles tip
rungs.words: When T_A_Full.DN (the done bit of T_A_Full: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on, the rung latches U_Hold (The unscrambler held: its accumulation is full) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_A_Full.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_A_Full.DN is on.
  2. OTL(U_Hold) Output Latch does: latches U_Hold on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: U_Hold stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: …and let it go again once the table has drained below the high eye: the gap between full and high is the hysteresis, so it does not chatter

pred.q: T_A_High.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: U_Hold is unlatched.

rungs.words: When T_A_High.DN (the done bit of T_A_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung unlatches U_Hold (The unscrambler held: its accumulation is full).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(T_A_High.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_A_High.DN is off.
  2. OTU(U_Hold) Output Unlatch does: unlatches U_Hold. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears U_Hold when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and U_Hold (The unscrambler held: its accumulation is full) is off, the rung turns U_Run (Unscrambler: run) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(U_Hold) Examine If Open asks: true when U_Hold is off.
  3. OTE(U_Run) Output Energize does: turns U_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: THE FILLER is fixed at its rated speed: the program only runs and holds it. When the capper's table has backed up to the filler's discharge (a cap jam), hold it before it runs blocked

pred.q: T_B_Full.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: F_Hold is left as it was. It stops at XIC(T_B_Full.DN).

rungs.words: When T_B_Full.DN (the done bit of T_B_Full: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on, the rung latches F_Hold (The filler held: the capper's accumulation has backed up to it) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_B_Full.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_B_Full.DN is on.
  2. OTL(F_Hold) Output Latch does: latches F_Hold on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: F_Hold stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: …and run it again as soon as the table drains below the high eye
rungs.words: When T_B_High.DN (the done bit of T_B_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung unlatches F_Hold (The filler held: the capper's accumulation has backed up to it).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(T_B_High.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_B_High.DN is off.
  2. OTU(F_Hold) Output Unlatch does: unlatches F_Hold. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears F_Hold when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: PRIME THE TABLE: at Start the tables are empty. Run the unscrambler first and start the filler once its table has backed up to the high eye, so the filler starts with a buffer to ride through the first hiccup

pred.q: Run is on and T_A_High.DN is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: F_Primed latches on.

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and T_A_High.DN (the done bit of T_A_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on, the rung latches F_Primed (The filler's table has filled to its high eye once since Start: the filler may run) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(T_A_High.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_A_High.DN is on.
  3. OTL(F_Primed) Output Latch does: latches F_Primed on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

rungs.head: Rung 17

rungs.ltr:

  2. OTU(F_Primed) Output Unlatch does: unlatches F_Primed. It only ever clears the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 18

pred.q: Run is on, F_Primed is off and F_Hold is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: F_Run is off. It stops at XIC(F_Primed).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, F_Primed (The filler's table has filled to its high eye once since Start: the filler may run) is on and F_Hold (The filler held: the capper's accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung turns F_Run (Filler: run) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(F_Primed) Examine If Closed asks: true when F_Primed is on.
  3. XIO(F_Hold) Examine If Open asks: true when F_Hold is off.
  4. OTE(F_Run) Output Energize does: turns F_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: THE CAPPER'S SPEED, the other side of the V: past the high eye the table is filling (after a jam), fast to clear it, 90 bpm
rungs.words: When T_B_High.DN (the done bit of T_B_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on, the rung puts 90 into C_Speed (Capper: speed reference, bottles a minute).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_B_High.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_B_High.DN is on.
  2. MOV(90,C_Speed) Move does: puts 90 into C_Speed. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: between the eyes: 69 bpm, faster than the filler, so the table runs down

pred.q: T_B_Low.DN is on and T_B_High.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: C_Speed is written.

rungs.words: When T_B_Low.DN (the done bit of T_B_Low: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is on and T_B_High.DN (the done bit of T_B_High: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung puts 69 into C_Speed (Capper: speed reference, bottles a minute).

  2. XIO(T_B_High.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_B_High.DN is off.
  3. MOV(69,C_Speed) Move does: puts 69 into C_Speed. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: short of the low eye: the filler's speed, 60 bpm, so the capper does not run itself empty and stop-start
rungs.words: When T_B_Low.DN (the done bit of T_B_Low: Debounce: the eye covered this long means the accumulation has backed up to it) is off, the rung puts 60 into C_Speed (Capper: speed reference, bottles a minute).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(T_B_Low.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_B_Low.DN is off.
  2. MOV(60,C_Speed) Move does: puts 60 into C_Speed. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 22

pred.q: Run is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: C_Run is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns C_Run (Capper: run) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(C_Run) Output Energize does: turns C_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: FAULTS: the lamp, and Start resets them
rungs.words: When either (U_Fault (Unscrambler: line-pressure fault) is on), (F_Fault (Filler: line-pressure fault) is on) or (C_Fault (Capper: line-pressure fault) is on), the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp: a machine has faulted) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(U_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when U_Fault is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(F_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when F_Fault is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(C_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when C_Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 24

pred.q: Start_PB is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: U_Reset is on, F_Reset is on and C_Reset is on.

rungs.words: When Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on, the rung turns U_Reset (Unscrambler: reset a line-pressure fault) on (and off whenever the rung is false), turns F_Reset (Filler: reset a line-pressure fault) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns C_Reset (Capper: reset a line-pressure fault) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(U_Reset) Output Energize does: turns U_Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(F_Reset) Output Energize does: turns F_Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. OTE(C_Reset) Output Energize does: turns C_Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
